skill.name: neurokit2
skill.description: Guides NeuroKit2 workflows for physiological signal processing, including ECG, EEG, EDA, RSP, PPG, EMG, EOG, HRV, event-related, and complexity analysis.
skill.summary: Analyze biosignals and physiological features with structured NeuroKit2 workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline references, and physiological terminology. One low-risk issue remains: the installation section recommends a mutable GitHub development zip URL. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or hidden execution intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the GitHub zipball/dev install example with a stable PyPI release or a commit-pinned URL.

content.value_statement: Biosignal projects need careful preprocessing, feature extraction, and interpretation across many signal types. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured NeuroKit2 workflows for reproducible physiological analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guide ECG and PPG preprocessing, peak detection, HRV analysis, and quality checks.
Support EEG power, microstate, channel quality, and MNE integration workflows.
Describe EDA, RSP, EMG, and EOG processing methods with key parameters.
Explain entropy, fractal, nonlinear, and event-related analysis workflows.
Provide multi-modal physiological analysis patterns using NeuroKit2 bio functions.
Point users to included reference files by signal type and method.
limitations: Does not diagnose medical conditions or replace clinical review.
Requires users to provide data, sampling rates, and study context.
May need external Python packages installed before examples can run.
Does not validate raw sensor quality without user-supplied evidence.

use_cases.title: Process experiment recordings
use_cases.description: Plan ECG, EDA, RSP, and EMG preprocessing for lab recordings with clear quality checks.

use_cases.title: Build biosignal features
use_cases.description: Select NeuroKit2 functions for HRV, entropy, microstates, and event-related features.

use_cases.title: Review signal methods
use_cases.description: Compare signal-processing choices and document analysis assumptions for teaching or peer review.

prompt_templates.title: Start ECG Analysis
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single cardiac recording.
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize how to process a 5-minute ECG recording with NeuroKit2. Include preprocessing, R-peak detection, HRV outputs, and quality checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose EDA and RSP Methods
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate method selection for autonomic and respiratory data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose NeuroKit2 functions for EDA and RSP data recorded at [sampling rate]. Explain parameters, expected outputs, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Event-Related Features
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced experimental analysis around stimulus markers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an event-related analysis plan for ECG and EDA around stimulus markers. Include epoch windows, baseline correction, artifacts, and reported features.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Modal Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a complete physiological study workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a multi-modal ECG, RSP, EDA, and EMG workflow for a stress study. Identify synchronization, feature extraction, statistics, and interpretation risks.

output_examples.input: I have 60 seconds of ECG sampled at 1000 Hz and need HRV features.
output: Use an ECG preprocessing pipeline before feature extraction.
Inspect R-peak detection and correct artifacts before HRV analysis.
Report recording duration because some HRV domains need longer windows.

output_examples.input: Compare ECG-derived HRV with PPG-derived HRV for a wearable study.
output: ECG is preferred when cardiac electrical timing is required.
PPG-HRV can be useful for time and frequency metrics when signal quality is strong.
Document pulse transit effects and validate against ECG when possible.

output_examples.input: Plan EEG microstate reporting for resting-state data.
output: Report the segmentation method, number of classes, and global explained variance.
Include duration, occurrence, coverage, and transition metrics.
Connect interpretation to neural network literature without overclaiming clinical meaning.

best_practices: Record sampling rate, sensor type, preprocessing choices, and artifact handling for every analysis.
Inspect signal quality visually before trusting automated features.
Match analysis windows and metrics to the research question and recording duration.
anti_patterns: Do not interpret physiological features as diagnoses without clinical validation.
Do not compare HRV metrics across sessions with different preprocessing choices.
Do not treat simulated examples as proof that real sensor data is clean.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users plan and explain NeuroKit2 workflows for physiological signal processing.

faq.question: Which signals does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers ECG, PPG, EEG, EDA, RSP, EMG, EOG, HRV, events, and complexity metrics.

faq.question: Can it run analysis by itself?
faq.answer: It guides workflows and examples. Users still need data, Python, and NeuroKit2 installed.

faq.question: Does it provide medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports research analysis and documentation, not diagnosis or treatment decisions.

faq.question: How should I start?
faq.answer: Provide signal type, sampling rate, recording duration, sensor context, and analysis goal.

faq.question: Can it handle multi-modal recordings?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for NeuroKit2 bio workflows and cross-signal interpretation.
